intro_payload.title: Passive Voice Mastery
intro_payload.subtitle: All Tenses + Modals + Special Cases + SBI PO Error Detection
learning_outcomes: Master exact Passive Voice formula across all convertible tenses
Know which tenses CANNOT be converted to Passive Voice (hidden exception)

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, socho tumhari mummy kitchen mein khana bana rahi hai. Tum do tarike se bol sakte ho: 'Mummy cooked the food' YA 'The food was cooked by mummy'. Dono ka matlab same hai, bas focus badal gaya. Batao dono sentence mein kya farak dikha?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir pehले mein 'Mummy' sabसे pehle aa rahi hai, lekin doosre mein 'food' pehले aa gaya! Aisa kyun?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut badhiya observation! Yahi toh Passive Voice ki poori kahani hai. Universal rule yaad rakho: Jab Object (jispe action hua) ko sentence ka Subject bana diya jaaye, aur asli Doer ko peeche 'by' ke saath ya bilkul hata diya jaaye, use Passive Voice kehte hain. 'The food was cooked by mummy' mein 'food' (jo pehले Object tha) ab naya Subject ban gaya hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh Object ko age laकर Subject banाना hi Passive Voice hai? Matlab jo pehле peeche tha wo aage aa gaya!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BPSC TRE Favorite: Bihar SCERT/BSEB ki grammar books mein Passive Voice ko 'Karma Vachya' (कर्म वाच्य) kaha jaata hai - kyunki isme 'Karma' (Object/Receiver) hi sentence ka star ban jaata hai, hero nahi. Yaad hai humne pichले chapter mein 'Karta Vachya' (Active Voice) seekha tha? BPSC TRE mein dono terms ko cross-question karte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Yaad hai sir! Karta Vachya matlab Doer wala Subject, aur Karma Vachya matlab Object wala Subject - simple hai ye toh!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ruko, ek important cheez batata hoon. Har Passive sentence mein 'by + Doer' likhna ZAROORI nahi hai! Jab Doer koi general/unknown/obvious insaan ho, toh use hata dete hain. Jaise: 'Rice is grown in Bihar' - yahaan 'by farmers' likhने ki zaroorat nahi kyunki ye obvious hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh agar pata hi hai ki kisने kiya (jaise farmers ne rice ugाया), toh 'by' likhने ka koi matlab nahi - samझ gaya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab poora formula samझते hain. Active: Subject + Verb + Object. Passive: Object (naya Subject) + be verb + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Doer (naya object, agar zaroorat ho). Sabसे important part yaad rakho - main verb hamesha V3 (third form) mein jaayegi, aur 'be' verb (is/am/are/was/were/been/being) tense ke hisaab se badalता hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, matlab jo verb pehле V1 ya V2 mein thi, wo Passive mein hamesha V3 ban jaayegi? Aur ek naya 'be' verb bhi add hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab yahin sabसे bada twist hai - konsa 'be' verb use karna hai, ye Active sentence ke ORIGINAL tense se decide hota hai, na ki Passive ke naye Subject se. Jaise 'Raju eats mango' (Simple Present) → be verb 'is/am/are' family se aayega: 'Mango is eaten by Raju.' Active tense hi Passive ke be-verb ki family decide karta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh pehле dekhна paडेga original sentence kaunse tense mein hai, phir usी tense ka 'be' verb use karна hai - ye toh bada useful trick hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tumne notice kiya? Jab Doer 'by' ke baad jaata hai, agar wo pronoun hai toh uska CASE badal jaata hai! Jaise: 'I' → 'me', 'he' → 'him', 'she' → 'her', 'we' → 'us', 'they' → 'them', 'who' → 'whom'. 'I wrote a letter' → 'A letter was written by me' (I nahi, me aayega).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Ye toh naya trap hai sir! Maine toh socha tha 'by I' likhते, but 'by me' sahi hai - ye toh exam mein zaroor pakड़ेंगे!

quiz_payload.explanation: Passive Voice ka formula hai: be verb + V3 (Past Participle). Verb hamesha V3 form mein hi rehती hai.

options.text: Naye Subject (jo pehले Object tha) se

quiz_payload.explanation: 'be' verb ka tense hamesha Active sentence ke original tense ke hisaab se decide hota hai - Simple Present ke liye is/am/are, Simple Past ke liye was/were, aadi.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Formula pakka ho gaya! Ab dekhते hain Present tenses mein Passive kaise banता hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab tense-by-tense Passive dekhते hain. Simple Present: Active - 'Raju writes a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter is written by Raju.' Formula: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject. 'is' singular ke liye, 'are' plural ke liye - naya Subject ki Number dekhкर decide karo.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, matlab ab check karна hoga naya Subject (jo Object tha) singular hai ya plural, phir is/are decide karna hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab Present Continuous: Active - 'Raju is writing a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter is being written by Raju.' Formula: Object + is/am/are + BEING + V3. Dekho, ek extra word 'being' aa gaya - ye continuous action dikhाने ke liye zaroori hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh 'being' bhi aata hai! Ye toh naya word hai, matlab continuous wale sentences mein hamesha 'being' lagाना paडेga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, continuous tenses mein hamesha 'being' aata hai. Ab Present Perfect: Active - 'Raju has written a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter has been written by Raju.' Formula: Object + has/have + BEEN + V3. Dhyan do 'been' aaya hai (being nahi) - ye perfect tenses ki pehchan hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'being' aur 'been' mein confuse ho jaata hoon - 'being' continuous ke liye, 'been' perfect ke liye, sahi samझा?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab yahin sabसे bada exception suno jo exam mein pucha jaata hai. Present Perfect Continuous - jaise 'Raju has been writing a letter for two hours' - iska koई STANDARD Passive form NAHI banता! Kyunki formula banega 'has been being written' jo bahut awkward aur grammatically avoid kiya jaata hai. Isliye is tense ko generally NOT converted maana jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Seriously sir? Matlab kuch tenses aise bhi hain jo Passive mein convert hi nahi hote? Ye toh bada bada trap ban sakता hai exam mein!

quiz_payload.explanation: Present Perfect Continuous ko Passive banाने par 'has been being + V3' jaisa awkward structure बनता hai, jo standard English mein avoid kiya jaata hai - isliye ye tense generally Passive mein convert nahi hota.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab Past family. Simple Past: Active - 'Raju wrote a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter was written by Raju.' Formula: Object + was/were + V3. 'was' singular ke liye, 'were' plural ke liye - bilkul present wale pattern jaisa, bas 'is/are' ki jagah 'was/were'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, toh bas 'is/am/are' ko 'was/were' se replace karна hai, baaki formula same rehता hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Past Continuous: Active - 'Raju was writing a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter was being written by Raju.' Formula: Object + was/were + BEING + V3. Yahaan bhi 'being' aata hai kyunki continuous action hai - bas 'is/are being' ki jagah 'was/were being'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Samझ gaya sir! Pattern toh same hai bas tense ke hisaab se 'is/am/are/was/were' badalते rehते hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi pakड़ा! Past Perfect: Active - 'Raju had written a letter before dinner.' → Passive - 'A letter had been written by Raju before dinner.' Formula: Object + HAD + BEEN + V3. Sabसे accha part - 'had' hamesha same rehта hai chahe Subject singular ho ya plural, isliye ye tense yaad karна sabसे easy hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wah, ye toh easy hai - 'had been' fix hai, koi confusion hi nahi singular-plural ka!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahin sabसे bada twist phir se suno - Past Perfect Continuous ('had been + V-ing') ko bhi standard Passive mein convert NAHI kiya jaata, exactly waise hi jaise Present Perfect Continuous ke saath hua tha. Formula banेगा 'had been being + V3' jo awkward hai, isliye exam mein ye considered NON-CONVERTIBLE hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha toh dono 'Perfect Continuous' wale tenses (Present aur Past) Passive mein convert nahi hote - ye pattern yaad rakh lunga sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab Future family. Simple Future: Active - 'Raju will write a letter.' → Passive - 'A letter will be written by Raju.' Formula: Object + WILL BE + V3. Yahaan bhi koई singular-plural ka jhanjhat nahi - 'will be' hamesha fix rehта hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, ye toh easy laग raha hai sir - 'will be' bas fixed hai sabके saath!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Ab Future Perfect: Active - 'Raju will have written the letter by evening.' → Passive - 'The letter will have been written by Raju by evening.' Formula: Object + WILL HAVE BEEN + V3. Ye bhi fixed combination hai, chahe Subject koई bhi ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye 'will have been' thoड़ा lamba lag raha hai but samझ aa gaya - bas fix combination yaad rakhна hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: BPSC ka favorite trap suno - Future Continuous ('will be + V-ing') aur Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been + V-ing') - dono ka bhi NO standard Passive form hota hai! Wajah wahi hai - 'will be being + V3' aur 'will have been being + V3' jaise structures itne awkward hain ki English mein avoid kiye jaate hain. Toh ab total CHAAR tenses ho gaye jo Passive mein convert nahi hote - Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect Continuous, Future Continuous, aur Future Perfect Continuous.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye to exam me pakka confuse karega sir! Toh matlab jitne bhi 'Continuous + Perfect' combination hai ya 'Continuous' jo Future mein hai, wo Passive nahi ban sakते?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab Modals ka Passive dekhते hain. Universal rule: Modal + BE + V3. Jaise: 'Raju can solve this puzzle.' → 'This puzzle can be solved by Raju.' 'Students must submit assignments.' → 'Assignments must be submitted by students.' Bas Modal ke turant baad 'be' laगाना hai, phir V3.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh Modal ke saath bhi 'be' fixed hi rehта hai, singular-plural ka koई farak nahi paडता?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi, Modal + be kabhi nahi badalता! Ab Modal Perfect Passive dekhो: Modal + HAVE BEEN + V3. Jaise: 'He should have completed the work.' → 'The work should have been completed by him.' Ye past ke regret/possibility ko Passive mein dikhाने ka tarika hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye 'have been' wala part toh humne pichले modules mein bhi dekha tha - matlab pattern repeat ho raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab Imperative sentences ka Passive dekhते hain - ye alag pattern follow karta hai. Order/Request: 'Close the door.' → 'Let the door be closed.' Formula: Let + Object + BE + V3. Request wale sentence mein 'Please' hoता hai toh 'You are requested to' use karте hain: 'Please help me' → 'You are requested to help me.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh normal order ke liye 'Let...be' formula, aur 'Please' wale request ke liye 'You are requested to' - dono alag hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab Interrogative (question) sentences ka Passive dekho. Yes/No question: 'Did Raju write the letter?' → 'Was the letter written by Raju?' - yahaan bhi 'Do/Does/Did' hata kar be-verb use karте hain. Wh-question: 'Who wrote this letter?' → 'By whom was this letter written?' - 'Who' Doer position mein tha toh 'by whom' ban jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'Who' se 'by whom' - ye toh naya twist hai! Matlab jab 'Who' Doer ho, toh Passive mein 'by whom' use karte hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ruko, ek aur important case dekhते hain - jab sentence mein DO Objects hon. Jaise: 'The teacher taught us grammar.' Yahaan 'us' (Indirect Object) aur 'grammar' (Direct Object) dono hain. Isko DO tarike se Passive bana sakते hain: 'We were taught grammar by the teacher.' YA 'Grammar was taught to us by the teacher.' Lekin exam mein PEHLA wala (Indirect Object ko Subject banाना) zyaादा preferred aur natural माना jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh do Objects wale sentence mein do Passive ban sakते hain, but 'Indirect Object ko Subject banाना' zyaादा sahi maana jaata hai - ye toh naya point hai mere liye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aakhri special case - Causative verbs (make/let/help) aur Perception verbs (see/hear/watch) ke saath ek chhota sa twist hai. Active mein: 'I saw him go.' / 'They made him work.' Jab inhe Passive banाते hain, toh bare infinitive (V1 bina 'to' ke) ke pehле 'to' add ho jaata hai: 'He was seen TO go.' / 'He was made TO work.' Ye chhota sa exception hai jo dhyan se yaad rakhна paडता hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, matlab Active mein 'to' nahi tha, lekin Passive banते hi 'to' add ho gaya? Ye toh sach mein exam mein trap ban sakता hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab hum enter kar rahe hain SBI PO/Bank PO level mein! Passive Voice se related teen bade traps hain - be-verb ka galat tense, V3 ki jagah V2/V1 ka use, aur missing/wrong preposition. Chalo ek-ek karke dekhते hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, Passive Voice mein toh itne parts hain - be verb, being, been, V3 - sabme se galti dhundना toh mushkil lagता hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ghabराओ mat, systematic approach seekhते hain. Trap 1 - Wrong Verb Form: Passive mein hamesha V3 chahiye, V2 nahi. 'The letter was wrote by him' - GALAT! Sahi hai 'The letter was written by him.' Ye SSC/Railway ka bahut common trap hai jahaan log V2 aur V3 confuse kar dete hain jab dono alag hote hain (write-wrote-written).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, matlab 'wrote' V2 hai aur 'written' V3 - Passive mein hamesha V3 wala 'written' hi aaएगा?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 2 - Subject-Verb (be-verb) Mismatch: Naya Subject (jo pehле Object tha) ki Number (singular/plural) check karके be-verb match karна hai. 'The books was placed on the table' - GALAT! 'Books' plural hai, isliye 'were' aayega: 'The books were placed on the table.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh, matlab ab naya Subject dekhкर is/are/was/were decide karna hai, na ki purане Subject se - ye toh main bhool sakта tha!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 3 - 'Being' vs 'Been' confusion: Continuous tenses mein 'being' aata hai, Perfect tenses mein 'been' aata hai. 'The work has being done' - GALAT! Sahi hai 'The work has been done.' (Present Perfect). Aur 'The work is been done' bhi GALAT hai, sahi hai 'The work is being done.' (Present Continuous). Dono ko mix karна exam ka common trap hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye 'being' aur 'been' toh dekhने mein bilkul alag nahi lagते, ye toh sach mein bahut confuse karने wala trap hai!

quiz_payload.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Passive Voice:
Statement I: The sentence 'The reports has been being prepared by the team since Monday' is the correct Passive form of 'The team has been preparing the reports since Monday.'
Statement II: 'The baby cried loudly' cannot be converted into Passive Voice because 'cried' is an intransitive verb.
Statement III: In the sentence 'By whom was this letter written?', the interrogative pronoun 'who' has correctly changed to 'whom' in the Passive form.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.text: Only I and III
Only II and III
Only I and II
Only I

quiz_payload.explanation: Statement I is WRONG - Present Perfect Continuous ('has been preparing') is one of the four tenses that CANNOT be converted into a standard Passive form, because it would require the awkward and grammatically avoided structure 'has been being prepared'. This tense is treated as non-convertible. Statement II is CORRECT - 'cry' is an intransitive verb with no object, so 'The baby cried loudly' cannot be converted into Passive Voice at all. Statement III is CORRECT - when 'who' (as Doer) is converted to Passive Voice, it correctly changes to 'whom' after 'by': 'By whom was this letter written?' is grammatically correct. Hence, only Statements II and III are correct - Answer (B).
